steps.note: The scarcest rule in the book: English has only on the order of a hundred palindromes of 3-10 letters, however big the book gets.
258 matching words in the list -- a hunt, and it has to run early or the later rules will have eaten most of them.

New rule, added near the beginning per Ian's request -- a fixed geometric count (4/page: 120 at 30 pages, 400 at 100), so it scales with the book automatically and needs no density tuning the way a keep_fraction rule normally does. PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction (0.983, aiming for roughly half the book's corners to deliberately contain E), unmeasured. Run bin/check.php before trusting it. Corners NOT claimed here are protected by a NoUnplannedCornerLetter invariant so no later rule's ordinary filler can accidentally land an E there.

Moved from much later in the chain, where the pool had already been thinned to 756 of its 1,064 unrestricted matches -- bin/check.php found demand (1,064 at keep_fraction 0.88) exceeding that. Here, right after the two rules that barely touch anything, it sees nearly the full catch. keep_fraction recalculated from the real cascade at this new position (pool ~11,749 entering this step) to cap demand around 646 -- comfortably under both the available count and Ian's 700-per-rule ceiling. Still worth confirming with bin/check.php.
~209 in the list.
Four letters and up: short words land in alphabetical order by chance constantly, and the minimum is also what lets the revealed word "any" through. Measured at 365 available.
Narrowed 2026-10-19 per Ian: the Y-exclusion cuts the raw catch from ~7,700 to ~1,900 and gives the reader a quick first check. keep_fraction retuned for the smaller catch.
PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction -- reduplicated words like this are rare, but the real count hasn't been measured against this book's dictionary yet. Run bin/check.php before trusting this number.
New rule, added 2026-10-19 with ContainsChRule and AlternatingConsonantVowelRule to take load off the >500-word steps. Huge, instantly checkable catch (~3,700 raw).
keep_fraction lowered from 0.93: real supply (3,424 matches) was 17x old demand (206), room to shift load off VowelRunRule, the chain's overloaded absorber.

Replaces plain "contains a double E" (ContainsDoubleERule, which matched too broadly). PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction, carried over unchanged from the old, looser rule -- the real catch here is smaller, so this will likely need to rise. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.

Replaces BothEndsInSetRule (single letter at each end, capped length) with a tighter four-letter check and no length cap. Measured with bin/check.php: real supply (5,399 matches) was 43x the 0.95 placeholder's demand (126), so keep_fraction was lowered to shift load off VowelRunRule, the chain's overloaded absorber.

Replaces VowelRunRule ("two vowels in a row anywhere"), which was a superset of DoubleEFewVowelsRule's catch -- any double-E word has two adjacent vowels by definition, the same supersedes-an-earlier-rule problem documented for the consonant_vowel_pattern/reversal rules elsewhere in config/README.md. Checking only the word's START avoids the overlap. bin/check.php found demand (1,854 at keep_fraction 0.75) well past both the available count (1,750) and Ian's 700-per-rule ceiling -- not starved, just too greedy. keep_fraction raised to cap demand around 677 at this step's new cascade position (pool ~7,963 after AlphabetAdjacentEndsRule moved earlier); the ~1,177 fewer cells removed here flow forward and land on MatchingNeighbourEndsRule (the absorber) unless redistributed further -- check whether that pushes IT over 700 next.
New rule, same load-shifting batch as EndsWithIngRule. ~5,500 raw matches.

New rule. PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction -- likely to be genuinely scarce (few words repeat so few distinct letters at this length), unmeasured against this book's dictionary. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.
New rule. PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction, unmeasured against this book's dictionary. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.

New rule -- nothing else in this simplified chain specifically targets length 10 (length_by_page, which used to cycle through it, was pulled earlier this session along with the rest of the positional family). Measured with bin/check.php: real supply (22,388 matches) was 300x the 0.96 placeholder's demand (74), the single biggest headroom in the chain, so keep_fraction was lowered substantially to shift load off VowelRunRule, the chain's overloaded absorber.
New rule, same load-shifting batch. ~2,100 raw matches; placed next to WordLength10Rule since both are length-flavoured.

Kept over SameVowelsOnPageRule, which was pulled: the two competed, each's accidental catch sometimes overlapping the other's deliberately-placed word (a cross-rule invariant collision, since fixed generically -- see PageSignaturePairRule::construct()) -- Ian preferred anagram pairs once it came to picking one. PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction, deliberately modest. Run bin/check.php before raising it.

New rule and new mechanism -- the vertical sibling of MatchingNeighbourEndsRule. Rewritten to pick two real words sharing a last letter up front (reserved, validated, placed as literals) rather than resolving the second word at fill time -- the fill-time version was how an orphaned half slipped through when several pair rules ran together. Uses the new Canvas::freeVerticalPairs(). PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction, deliberately modest first run. Run bin/check.php before raising it.

Reinstated as a trial, per Ian's intuition that splitting a pair into a plain left cell plus a letter-dependent right cell might hide a problem. That intuition was right (fixed: now picks two real words up front, reserved, placed as literals). Capped to a small keep_fraction like its sibling pair rules, rather than left as the absorber -- EVERY literal-placed pair carries a small risk of colliding with an unrelated neighbour once actually placed (the same risk AnagramPairOnPageRule always had), and with it absorbing an unbounded leftover, SOME collision across hundreds of pairs became near-certain on every single attempt, discarding the whole thing each time. VowelRunRule (below) is the absorber now -- ordinary filler has a real fallback (try another dictionary word) that a committed literal pair doesn't.

New rule, Ian's second brainstormed addition. Unlike the other pair rules, needs no SPECIFIC matching word -- any 9-letter and any 3-letter word qualify -- so both halves are ordinary cells with full dictionary fallback, not a fragile reserved pair. Guarded (construction-time check + NoLengthAdjacentToOpposingLiteral invariant) against accidentally orphaning AnagramPairOnPageRule/SameEndingVerticalPairRule/MatchingNeighbourEndsRule's own fragile pairs; deliberately does NOT guard against overlapping its own matches, since clustering is the explicitly wanted behaviour here. PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction (0.97, matching its sibling pair rules' tier), unmeasured. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.

New rule, added to take load off VowelRunRule (the absorber): density-correct target is ~7 matches/page (700 cells at 100 pages, per Ian's own calibration), but VowelRunRule alone was absorbing 33/page even after round-2 tuning. Doubled consonants are one of English's most common patterns and barely overlap RepeatedLetterRule (needs 4+ anywhere, not 2 adjacent) or VowelRunRule (consonants only, vowels excluded). PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction (0.73, hand-traced to land ~274 cells), unmeasured. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.

Third of three new rules added together to bring VowelRunRule's absorbed share down from ~33/page toward the ~7/page density target. Distinct from StartsWithTwoVowelsRule (checks the first TWO letters, nothing about the last) and from AlphabetAdjacentEndsRule (alphabet adjacency, not vowel-ness). PLACEHOLDER keep_fraction (0.52, hand-traced to land ~228 cells), unmeasured. Run bin/check.php before trusting it.

Reinstated as the chain's absorber (the last step with a keep_fraction) -- removed earlier this session for being a superset of DoubleEFewVowelsRule's catch, but that concern was about wasting a MID-chain rule's own turn on redundant matches. As the deliberate last-resort catch-all, a broad catch is exactly the point: ordinary ambiguous filler, with real fallback if one candidate word doesn't fit a cell, is what should be absorbing the unbounded leftover -- not a committed literal pair.

Holds back a handful of seven-letter words with no adjacency or covering logic at all -- just an ordinary flat claim on free cells, shaped to survive and then be swept by the final step. Replaces the reveal + knight's-move finale (see config/README.md for why those are currently out). See lib/Rules/DecoyLengthRule.php. Switched from length 5 to length 7 after length-5 ran out of surviving words to hand out during a real build -- check bin/check.php's "by word length" table before trusting this one either.
Clears the decoy words held back above -- and any other seven-letter word still standing, since nothing above this point spares them.
